title: Nvidia sets options-trading record after CEO comeback. Here are the big trades
summary: Nvidia break record for single stock options volume
body: One of the most dramatic about-faces in corporate America's history, Jensen Huang's return to the helm of AI chipmaker Nvidia spurred an equally historic record in the options market. More than 11 million options contracts traded on Nvidia stock Monday, the most active single day of trading for the stock's options in history. That outpaces the 9 million options traded on the Invesco QQQ Trust , and compares to 14 million traded on the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) . Despite Nvidia's monstrous 31% rally and options volume that was more than five times the 30-day average, positioning in the flows was not abnormally bullish. Of the top 10 trades by dollar amount, two big put sales stood out, but there were no likely outright call buys, based on data from Barchart and SpotGamma. If there was speculative call-buying, it was dwarfed by big trades between the 160 and 170 strikes, where four million options traded for almost $2 billion. Nvidia closed near $165. "People are mostly just trying to collect a lot of premiums through short vol trades and rolls once they heard about Jensen Huang, take advantage of the vol drop more than anything else," Jason DeLorenzo, founder of Volland, an options-analytics software, said by phone. "It seems like options traders were all repricing, which created record volume, but did not create any obvious one-sidedness." Just under 6.7 million calls traded versus 4.3 million puts, according to Cboe LiveVol data. About 2.4 million calls were likely initiated by buyers, compared with 1.6 million purchasing puts, exchange data show. Open interest in calls was highest at the 170-strike, while open interest in puts was highest at the 150-strike, Barchart data show.

title: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Nvidia stock with Jensen Huang back as CEO
summary: CNBC's Jim Cramer said Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO could help revive the chipmaker's battered stock.
body: Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO , CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday. "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the " Mad Money " host said. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now." Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure. "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he said. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary." Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership. "If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer said. Still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates. Those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The New York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he said the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock currently trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet. "There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said. "These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. title: Fed's John Williams indicates higher interest rates likely 'over time' to address inflation
summary: The influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027.
body: New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said Monday that policymakers have more work to do to bring inflation under control, though he indicated that further action can unfold over time as the economy continues to grow. In remarks consistent with previous statements , the influential central banker expressed confidence that inflation will get closer to the Fed's 2% target in 2027 before hitting the goal the following year. He also said that while artificial intelligence is pressuring prices, there's "little evidence" it will be the source of more persistent inflation. "But getting inflation back to 2% is 100% essential," he said in remarks at the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis. There is still work to do to get that done." The comments come at a delicate moment for monetary policy, as the economy continues to grow and inflation stays well above the Fed's goal. Fed officials have differed over how quickly to raise rates, with some advocating more aggressive action while others, including Williams, have emphasized a measured approach. Williams ascribed the current inflation pressures to the conflict in Iran, demand for goods associated with the AI build-out and tariffs, the effects of which he said "have largely abated" as a source of pressure. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence that inflation will subside substantially in 2027 even as economic growth remains robust and unemployment edges lower. The Federal Open Market Committee next meets on Dec. 8-9, with markets fully pricing in a quarter percentage point interest rate increase from the current target range of 3.75%-4%. The remarks from Williams are expected to be the last major policy statement from any Fed official before the December decision. "Monetary policy cannot move ships or reopen pipelines and refineries, but it can — and must — ensure that these shocks do not lead to broader or persistent inflationary dynamics or erode well-anchored inflation expectations," Williams said, according to his prepared remarks. Williams did not explicitly address the December meeting expectations, instead pointing to the statement released after the prior FOMC meeting in late October that said the "accumulation of more information" will help decide the future policy path. "The data that we have received since then show that the economy has remained strong and that inflation has continued to run too high," he said.

title: Jensen Huang cheered by Nvidia employees after return, pledges to be a better CEO
summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a note to employees on Nov. 8 and resigned as CEO on Nov. 12.
body: The mood inside Nvidia was jubilant as CEO Jensen Huang walked in on Monday to chants of his first name and three floors of cheering employees, according to a video shared with CNBC. "Thank you all for the second chances," Huang said to the crowd. "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around." Nvidia announced on Monday that Huang had been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately. It was a dramatic turn in the chaos that's enveloped the chip giant and the entire tech trade since reports surfaced that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy . The reports sparked renewed investigations into the smuggling of restricted Nvidia chips into China. Huang admitted to an affair in a note to employees on Nov. 8 and resigned as CEO on Nov. 12. The New York Times and Reuters subsequently reported that Huang had relationships with two employees, one of whom was a direct report. On Monday, cupcakes were circulating at the office with "Jensen is back" written on them, according to a person inside the company who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. There was a sense of excitement among employees, as well as frustration over how the events of the last two weeks unfolded, the person said, adding that last Wednesday's all-hands meeting was a turning point. A side-by-side photo was circulated internally of an all-hands meeting hosted by Huang, contrasted with the most recent meeting with a group of executives and board members sitting on stage, according to the person. Now, all eyes are on the board, which said just last week that Huang would not be coming back . "It's embarrassing for the board," said a former Nvidia employee who was at the company for more than 15 years, who asked not to be named in order to share insight into the company. "It's likely that the board will change and some people may step down, some people may be replaced," the former employee said. They added that many employees "felt that the board acted too hastily." President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he played a large role in Huang's return, and that he spoke to the board "directly and indirectly." Trump called into the board meeting that was held on Sunday, CNBC confirmed. WATCH: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Jensen Huang

body: The direct price signal for BTC and ETH is small. The advisory frees up some capital on the balance sheets of crypto-native venues but doesn't create new demand for either coin . Spot ETF flows shouldn't feel it. The listed company with the most obvious stake is COIN, since Coinbase runs a CFTC-registered derivatives exchange, though the benefit is about capital efficiency rather than earnings. More broadly, it's another sign that US regulators are steadily folding crypto into existing market structure, which supports institutional sentiment more than it moves prices. US derivatives venues can now count some of their crypto toward operating reserves, but the haircuts, the cash-only liquidity floor and the wrong-way risk test keep that allowance modest. US derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can now count some of the bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins on their balance sheets toward their regulatory financial reserves, according to a staff advisory from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission published on 23 November. The crypto must be marked down first, and it cannot be used for the most liquid part of the requirement. Under CFTC rules, designated contract markets (DCMs), swap execution facilities (SEFs) and derivatives clearing organisations (DCOs) must hold enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs. Until now, only cash and traditional financial assets counted. CFTC Staff Letter 26-31, signed by the acting heads of the Division of Market Oversight and the Division of Clearing and Risk, says staff would not object to bitcoin and ether being counted after a haircut of at least 20%, with a 2% minimum haircut for payment stablecoins. Other crypto that is not readily marketable and does not qualify as a payment stablecoin would generally take a 100% haircut, so in practice it counts for nothing. The bigger constraint is liquidity. Part of the 12-month buffer must be held in unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities: at least three months of costs for SEFs and at least six months for DCMs and DCOs. Staff said crypto, stablecoins included, is neither cash under GAAP nor a highly liquid security, so it cannot fill that portion. For a DCM or DCO, that means crypto can cover at most the other half of the year, and each dollar of bitcoin counts as no more than 80 cents. Clearinghouses must also factor liquidity risk into their haircuts and review them monthly. Entities must also weigh wrong-way risk, the danger that a slide in crypto prices arrives at the same time as losses in their own business. For crypto-focused venues, whose trading revenue tends to fall when the market does, that could argue for haircuts well above the minimum. The advisory does not cover the default resources a clearinghouse holds against a member failure, and it is non-binding staff guidance rather than a Commission rule. Even so, it carries the 20% and 2% haircuts already set for futures brokers in March, which mirror the SEC's treatment of broker-dealers, over to the trading venues and clearinghouses themselves. That extends the CFTC's gradual move to bring crypto inside its existing rulebook rather than writing a separate one. Your market education doesn't end here. Singapore's economy grew much faster than first estimated in the third quarter, and the government responded by sharply raising its 2026 growth forecast to around 6%, underlining how strongly the city-state is riding global demand for AI-related electronics. Gross domestic product expanded 6.1% from a year earlier in the July to September quarter, well above the advance estimate of 5.4% and beating the 5.6% expected by economists in a Reuters poll. On a seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis, the economy grew 1.5%, up from the advance reading of 1.1% and ahead of forecasts of around 1.3%. That leaves third-quarter momentum matching the second quarter's revised 1.5% pace rather than slowing, as the early data had suggested. The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, renamed from the Ministry of Trade and Industry in October, lifted its 2026 growth forecast to around 6.0% from a previous range of 4.5% to 5.5%. It said the external demand outlook for the year has improved since its August assessment. For 2027, the ministry expects growth to slow to a range of 2.5% to 4.5%. Trade figures tell a similar story. Enterprise Singapore raised its 2026 forecast for non-oil domestic exports, known as NODX, to growth of 30% to 32%, a striking pace for a key export gauge. It expects NODX growth to ease to 5% to 7% in 2027. The advance estimate showed growth led by manufacturing, particularly the electronics, precision engineering, transport engineering and general manufacturing clusters, which outweighed declines in chemicals and biomedical output. The Monetary Authority of Singapore has said AI-related demand remained firm through the quarter, with any softness in electronics output more likely reflecting capacity constraints in global supply chains than weaker orders. The full sector breakdown with today's release will show which industries drove the upward revision. A large revision between the advance and final readings is not unusual for Singapore. The advance figure is built largely from July and August data, and last year the third-quarter estimate was also revised up sharply, followed by a forecast upgrade. The forecasts also carry a warning. Growth of around 6% this year is expected to give way to as little as 2.5% in 2027, as the export boom normalises and comparisons with this year's strong base get tougher. Concentration in AI-related electronics leaves Singapore exposed if technology investment slows, and new US licensing requirements on advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore and four other countries add a further source of uncertainty for the trade hub. The data will feed into the Monetary Authority of Singapore's next policy review, due no later than January 29. The central bank manages policy through the exchange rate rather than interest rates, and stronger growth gives it more reason to keep its current settings. Your market education doesn't end here. In the week to November 13, U.S. refinery utilization rose to 95.7%, and gasoline inventories climbed by 5.2 million barrels to 215.9 million barrels, according to the EIA's weekly report . That build was more than three times the 1.6 million barrels analysts polled by Reuters had expected. Distillate stocks rose by 1.6 million barrels to 104.9 million. Related: America's Refiners Drowned Their Own Gasoline Windfall The two fuels are now on opposite ends of the five-year range. Shares of both companies have doubled this year, according to the Motley Fool. The agency expects global refinery runs to rise from a seasonal low of 81.3 million bpd in October to 84.7 million bpd in December. body: ConocoPhillips to Exit Norway in $4.43 Billion Deal with Vaar Energi What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… For the first time since 2009, the Conference of the Parties ended without a deal to advance an energy transition as participating countries failed to agree on key aspects of that deal. Disagreements were most notable in financial commitments for developing countries and in blaming oil and gas for climate change. COP31 was arguably doomed from the start. Financial commitments are a central part of the talks, with wealthy Western countries pledging billions in energy-transition assistance to developing nations in Asia, South America, and Africa, either as grants or loans. Yet transition advancements have fallen short of expectations—and not only in developing nations. The bigger problem, however, is that money has started to run out amid two wars that have strained state coffers across the world. The European Union has been the most generous climate finance donor and lender globally for years, but money has been tight lately, with soaring fuel prices, soaring gas prices, and a shortage of refining capacity. This year, the EU’s most pressing problems have ironically swung to those same fossil fuels that it is trying to phase out and get a commitment from the rest of the world to do the same. Solving these hydrocarbon problems requires heavy spending in the form of direct subsidies and tax cuts to cushion the blow. There is, in short, no money for COP31 commitments. He headed utility equity research at a major brokerage house and… Perhaps you have heard about the daily “duck curve” in electricity markets. Abundant daytime solar energy displaces higher-cost forms of power generation during daylight hours. It creates a price chart for power that resembles the belly and neck of a duck. In the old days,, as the sun went down, gas-fired turbines (CTs) were called upon to provide power for shoulder periods of daily electricity demand when power needs were still elevated. albeit trending down. What’s changed? A few electricity markets with extensive solar and battery penetration, like California, are using their gas-fired CTs a lot less, because they are being displaced by cheaper electricity from batteries. Said differently, in wholesale power markets, batteries are underpricing gas-fired generation. Obviously, this is disruptive, meaning simply that the owner of a particular type of power generation suddenly finds its assets impaired, or as we call it, stranded. Many recent articles have focused on the unrelenting downward cost of solar, onshore wind, and batteries. This is all true. But will it be disruptive? One way to tell is by looking at changes in capital investment. No utility executive wants to lose money on a new big power plant or transmission line. According to the EIA, the US will add 86 GW of capacity in 2026, 89% of which will be solar and battery, and only 7% gas-fired. (The 2025 additions were similar in terms of fuel mix.) We are seeing a big upswing in demand for electricity. AI just turbocharged it. Looking at those projections, one might conclude that gas is being displaced by renewables, but we sure can’t see it. Gas-fueled electricity production has held steady. It simply doesn't appear to matter that renewables provide cheaper energy, at least for now. Our best analogy is telegraph (a legacy technology) vs telephone (disruptive technology) in the early twentieth century. Everyone knows how the story ends. But few remember that these two competing technologies co-existed happily for several decades because there was adequate demand and revenue for both. And then the former simply went away. (The same happened with gas lighting, which co-existed with electric lighting for decades before expiring.) And that’s our best guess for fossil-fired generation. In the near to intermediate term, it will coexist happily with renewable technologies because of continuing growth in power demand. Related: What Is Trump Up To Bombing Iran’s Qeshm Island? But this is not to say there will be no revenue disruption at all for utilities, just that people are looking for it in the wrong place, in the big power generating assets. Potential disruption could come from three sources. First, the rapid increase in gas generation build-out adds many large businesses like data centers to the domestic market. This increased demand will inevitably add upward pressure on gas prices. Also, if the US continues to export increasing quantities of LNG such that it becomes priced on a world market like oil, that too would add another level of unattractive price volatility. Both trends bear watching. Second, there is potential for disruption in the utility asset class that is considered the lowest risk: transmission and distribution. title: Prospectiva hits rich copper zone at São Francisco
summary: The new hole supports Prospectiva’s interpretation that the copper mineralization extends deeper towards the east.
body: The new hole supports Prospectiva’s interpretation that the copper mineralization extends deeper towards the east. New drilling by Prospectiva Resources (TSXV: PSVA) at the São Francisco project in northeastern Brazil has produced its most significant copper intersection yet ahead of an initial resource estimate. The stock surged. Step-out hole SF_26_006 cut 10.02 metres grading 11.75% copper, 0.87 gram gold per tonne and 1.09% zinc from 104.98 metres downhole, Prospectiva said Monday in a statement . The hole is about 60 metres northeast of hole SF_26_003, which yielded 7.15 metres at 4.78% copper from 85.85 metres downhole. “We are continuing to intersect significant zones of massive and semi-massive copper sulphides, with high-grade mineralisation now demonstrated across successive drill holes,” CEO Dan James said. Prospectiva shares jumped 36% to 58¢ Monday afternoon on the TSX Venture Exchange, valuing the explorer at about $15 million (US$10.4 million). The stock has traded between 38.5¢ and $1 in the past year. The new hole, in the Borborema mineral belt, supports Prospectiva’s interpretation that the copper mineralization extends deeper towards the east. The company is drilling along a 3-km prospective corridor as it works towards an initial resource next year. Reported intervals are lengths along the drill hole; their true widths remain unknown. Prospectiva has completed nine planned diamond drill holes this year. Assay results have been received for the first six holes, with results from the remaining completed holes pending. Two drill rigs are now turning and drilling is expected to complete by Dec. 31. Toronto-based Prospectiva acquired the project in early 2026. Yamana Gold discovered the copper-gold system in 2019 and completed about 5,900 metres of historical diamond drilling. The licences passed to Pan American Silver (TSX, NYSE: PAAS) following its acquisition of Yamana in 2023 before being transferred to Prospectiva. Earlier drilling included 7.5 metres grading 6.41% copper and 0.36 gram gold per tonne in historical hole SF_006. That hole is distinct from the newly reported SF_26_006. Prospectiva’s current drilling is testing extensions of known mineralized zones and targets identified by electromagnetic surveys. Prospectiva interprets São Francisco as a volcanogenic massive sulphide-style system: sulphide-rich mineralization associated with ancient volcanic activity that has since been folded and altered by heat and pressure. Prospectiva is using drill-core measurements and geophysical surveys to refine the deposit’s shape and guide further drilling.

body: When gold prices rise, many people delay their purchases and wait for a fall. When prices drop, others wait to see if they will fall further. But how can buyers understand which way the market might move? US economic reports can offer some clues. Inflation, employment, economic growth and interest-rate decisions can all influence international gold prices. These reports follow a schedule. Buyers and investors can use release dates to prepare for potential market moves. However, a report's release date does not tell us whether gold prices will rise or fall. The key is to compare the actual figures with market expectations. Gold is traded internationally in US dollars. Its price is therefore linked to the strength of the dollar, US interest rates and government bond yields. When US interest rates rise, bonds and other interest-bearing investments become more attractive. Gold does not pay interest. Some investors may therefore sell gold and move their money into these assets. This can push gold prices down. The opposite can happen when interest rates fall, or investors expect rate cuts. A weaker dollar and lower bond yields can also support gold prices. Recent market movements offer an example. In October, US consumer inflation rose 0.4 per cent, above the market forecast of 0.3 per cent, according to the US Bureau of Labour Statistics (BLS). Core inflation also rose 0.3 per cent, above the expected 0.2 per cent. The figures strengthened the dollar and pushed Treasury yields higher. Spot gold fell 2.7 per cent to $4,028.39 per ounce on November 10, Reuters reported. Several US agencies publish economic reports every month. Here are eight releases scheduled between late November and mid-December 2026 that could influence the gold market. The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index every month. It measures how consumers feel about the economy, job opportunities and their financial situation. A higher-than-expected reading could suggest that the US economy remains strong. This may reduce expectations of interest-rate cuts and put pressure on gold prices. The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) publishes Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data in its Personal Income and Outlays report. Investors pay close attention to Core PCE. It excludes food and energy prices because they tend to fluctuate more. For example, if the expected monthly core inflation figure is 0.2 per cent but the actual figure reaches 0.4 per cent, investors may expect fewer Fed rate cuts. The dollar and bond yields could rise, putting pressure on gold. Lower-than-expected inflation could have the opposite effect. It may increase expectations of rate cuts and support gold prices. The BEA is also scheduled to publish its second estimate of US GDP growth for the third quarter of 2026. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total value of goods and services produced in an economy. It helps investors assess economic growth. Stronger-than-expected growth could reduce expectations of interest-rate cuts. This may put downward pressure on gold. Weaker growth could increase those expectations and support gold prices. The BLS publishes the Job Openings and Labour Turnover Survey (JOLTS). It provides data on job vacancies, hiring, and workers leaving their jobs. body: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO triggered a sharp rally in the company’s shares as well as the broader tech market. However, some commentators said the move is a net positive, but risks remain, and the outcome of the government investigation will provide greater clarity on the long-term outlook. NVDA stock rose 31.5% on Monday after the Nvidia board announced the return of Huang, and gained a further 0.5% in overnight trading. Intel (AMD), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO) and iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) gained sharply as well but fell in overnight trading. Hyperscaler Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOGL) kept their gains overnight. “The NVIDIA board’s brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed,” said a joint statement by the Select Committee on China, Select Committee on Intelligence, and Foreign Affairs Committee, which is investigating Nvidia and Huang over the spy crisis. Huang and Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter will appear for hearings on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively. “We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities," the statement read. The California state and the Securities and Exchange Commission are also investigating the AI chip giant for various alleged infringements. Huang’s reappointment marks a dramatic turn of events. He was ousted after his multiple affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, came to light, and the Nvidia board had said last week that it had no plans to bring him back. The board reversed its position on Monday, hours after President Donald Trump posted in support of Huang’s reinstatement. The development reinforces that Huang is a special leader and Nvidia is a special company but also flags questions, said Wharton professor Mohamed A. El-Erian. “While today’s news answers one set of questions, it raises another set that, similarly, ranges from the narrow (Nvidia’s governance process) to the broad (implications for markets, presidential put, government intervention, national champions, etc.),” he said in an X post. Noted Nvidia critic and “Big Short Investor” Michael Burry said Nvidia is hardly out of the woods. “So $NVDA is weaker, more craven than even I thought. @TheJusticeDept stay on that antitrust case. @SECGov keep digging into that accounting. Godspeed,” he said in an X post. On the other hand, Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster said he was not surprised with the stock's sharp rally on Monday. “The reason is the fundamentals of the AI trade are stronger than what we thought on Nov 5 with Nvidia raising next years guide by 5%. Even with China revenue that will get scrubbed the underlying message remains: we’re early in AI,” he said in an X post. “$NVDA is still 11% lower than post-Blue Wave selloff. I think it’s fair it closes that gap back to $182,” he said. CNBC’s Jim Cramer said: “Look it was a hasty investigation and then a hanging. Jensen welcome back.” On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for NVDA climbed higher in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone. At least 64% of nearly 25,000 traders who voted in an ongoing Stocktwits poll said they feel more bullish about Nvidia after Huang’s return. Fifteen percent said they felt the same as before and 12% voted saying it is too early to tell. “From the companies perspective it's good news.. but let's see what happens when the investigation gets fully underway, 1st week of December will be interesting,” a trader commented. “Honestly I expect there is more we don't know yet. im not ready to jump back in personally.” Despite Monday’s rally, NVDA stock remained 11.3% lower year to date.

body: Broadcom shares have surrendered most of their gains for the year as investors assess competition in custom AI chips and pressure on margins. The company reported rapid growth in AI semiconductor sales and raised its full-year AI revenue forecast, while analysts maintain a Strong Buy consensus rating. Broadcom shares have given up most of their gains for the year, leaving investors weighing whether it is time to buy after the pullback. The decline comes amid a wider selloff in artificial intelligence stocks and concerns about competition in custom AI chips. Margins are also under pressure. Broadcom expects AI products to account for a growing share of sales, affecting gross margins. Marvell Technology's partnership with Alphabet's Google to develop custom AI chips has added to concerns about competition. Broadcom, meanwhile, says demand for its own accelerators is growing. Broadcom reported third-quarter revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% from a year earlier. Revenue growth accelerated from 29% in the first quarter and 48% in the second. Its AI semiconductor business grew 221% from a year earlier and 54% from the previous quarter. The business generated more than $16.7 billion in revenue, more than tripling from a year earlier. Broadcom has six customers for its custom AI accelerators, known as XPUs. Those customers are expanding deployments of their accelerators. XPU shipments rose more than 3.5 times and accounted for approximately 73% of AI semiconductor revenue in the third quarter. AI networking revenue grew more than 2.5 times. Broadcom expects fourth-quarter AI revenue of $21.7 billion, up 236% from a year earlier. The forecast reflects higher accelerator shipments for Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and Meta. The company expects both XPU and AI networking revenue to triple from a year earlier. Management raised its FY26 AI revenue forecast to approximately $58 billion, representing 186% growth. Broadcom expects AI revenue to reach $115 billion in FY27 and $230 billion in FY28. The company says it has secured the supply needed to support those targets. Third-quarter operating income rose 92% from a year earlier, outpacing revenue growth despite pressure from changes in the business mix. Management expects earnings per share to exceed $30 by FY28. Beyond AI semiconductors, Broadcom expects demand in broadband and server storage to support its other chip businesses. VMware is also expanding its opportunity in enterprise AI. Infrastructure software revenue reached $8.8 billion in the third quarter, up 29% from a year earlier. Annual recurring revenue, the amount generated by ongoing subscriptions and contracts, grew 15%. Broadcom expects fourth-quarter FY26 revenue of $34.8 billion, up 93% from a year earlier. It forecasts an operating margin of approximately 66%. The stock trades at 19.3 times forward earnings. Analysts project earnings per share of $17.31 in FY27, up 70%. Analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on Broadcom shares and an average price target of $519.11.
